name: Germinal centre
summary: A germinal centre forms inside a B-cell follicle a few days into an immune response. In the dark zone, B cells that have met their antigen divide fast and mutate their antibody genes; in the light zone they test the new antibody against antigen held by follicular dendritic cells, and the best binders win help from Tfh cells. The winners leave as plasma cells or memory B cells.
description: One germinal centre inside a B-cell follicle, as a large oval. The dark zone, packed with dividing B cells, is on the left; the light zone, with follicular dendritic cells and helper T cells, is on the right. A ring of resting B cells surrounds it, and arrows on the right show memory B cells and plasma cells leaving. Seven cells are labelled.

residents.note: Resting B cells pushed aside by the growing germinal centre form the mantle zone around it.
Divides and mutates its antibody genes in the dark zone, then moves to the light zone to be tested; it cycles between the two zones many times.
Tingible body macrophages swallow the many germinal centre B cells that die after failing selection.
Its long processes hold antigen, bound by antibody and complement, on which B cells in the light zone test their antibody.
Gives survival and division signals (CD40L, IL-21) to the B cells that show it the most antigen.
Leaves the germinal centre to recirculate, ready for a faster response next time.
Leaves the germinal centre to make high-affinity antibody, in the medulla or in the bone marrow.

regions.name: Dark zone
regions.summary: The half of the germinal centre packed with dividing B cells. Here they multiply quickly, and their antibody genes pick up mutations, so each new B cell carries a slightly different antibody.
happens: Germinal centre B cells divide rapidly.
Mutations build up in the genes for the antibody's binding site (somatic hypermutation), so daughter cells bind antigen more or less tightly than their parent.
B cells are drawn here by CXCL12, made by reticular cells of the dark zone, and later move to the light zone to be tested.

regions.name: Light zone
regions.summary: The half of the germinal centre where B cells are tested. Each tries to capture antigen held on follicular dendritic cells and show it to Tfh cells; those that capture the most get the help they need to survive.
happens: B cells capture antigen from the processes of follicular dendritic cells with their mutated receptor.
Tfh cells give survival and division signals (CD40L, IL-21) to the B cells that present the most antigen.
Selected B cells return to the dark zone for another round, or leave as plasma cells or memory B cells; the rest die and are swallowed by macrophages.
